type: method: overwrite an existing same-type header-table record with the clone block
structure: Registering a clone without growing the header table or shifting the file

location.offset: a chosen type-92 header-table entry whose blob >= the clone block

meaning: Because relocation is reflection-driven (igz.loader.relocation-table), a same-type record in an already-registered slot needs no new relocation data. Growing the header table to register a clone shifts every object 32 bytes and desynchronises the load (froze at 1 036/21 680 records), so registration must not move anything. `igz clone-entity --overwrite <T>` writes the clone block over an existing type-92 table record T (rebasing block-internal pointers to T, zeroing the blob leftover, incrementing the refcounts of the shared objects the clone points at), leaving T`s table entry and every other byte untouched. On the tutorial, target 0x3EDEFC (chosen with igz pick-overwrite-target: blob 0x500, 0 external references into its interior) yields a VALID plan whose diff against the original is exactly the 0x2A8 clone block plus five 4-byte refcount words at the shared externals (0x187BF0, 0x187E74, 0x188CC0, 0x188CDC, 0x1893EC); the file length is identical. This is the registration path to test next; it sacrifices one benign type-92 record to host a duplicate of the spawn entity.

evidence.probe: ssa-archive igz clone-entity --overwrite (static, entity-overwrite-plan.json) + byte diff
evidence.summary: VALID plan; only [0x3EDEFC,0x3EE3FC) and 5 refcount words differ; file length unchanged; clone owner and physics recognised at the target
129 type-92 table entries with blob >= 0x2A8; 0x3EDEFC has 0 external references into its blob

CONTRADICTION of the "registration is enough" hypothesis: the in-place overwrite onto 0x3EDEFC loaded with the file length unchanged and nothing shifted, and the ORIGINAL spawn constructed normally (class pointer 0x80486514), but the load still froze on "Loading" and the clone`s position (99.73) was absent from MEM1 entirely — construction hangs before reaching/finishing the duplicated record. Registering a same-type record in a valid slot is necessary but NOT sufficient; duplicating a type-92 entity is blocked by a deeper construction constraint (candidate: the type-92 walk iterates children by the blob/size or a count and mis-parses the zeroed leftover, or a duplicated record conflicts on an identity/handle/dependency that in-place M2 mutation never triggers).
